DuPont analysis: purpose and uses
杜邦分析：目的与用途
Back:
The DuPont system breaks down ROE into component ratios. Uses: it enables meaningful evaluation of different aspects of performance affecting ROE; identifies reasons for changes in ROE over time; explains differences in ROE across companies; directs management to areas to improve ROE; and shows how the various categories of ratios influence owners' return.
杜邦分析体系将 ROE 分解为若干构成比率。用途：对影响 ROE 的各方面业绩进行有意义的评估；识别 ROE 随时间变化的原因；解释不同公司之间 ROE 的差异；指引管理层明确改进 ROE 的方向；并展示各类比率如何影响所有者回报。

Front:
Two-way and three-way DuPont decomposition
两因素与三因素杜邦分解
Back:
Two-way: ROE = (Net income / Average total assets) × (Average total assets / Average shareholders' equity) = ROA × Financial leverage. Three-way: ROE = (Net income / Revenue) × (Revenue / Average total assets) × (Average total assets / Average equity) = Net profit margin × Asset turnover × Financial leverage.
两因素：ROE＝（净利润/平均总资产）×（平均总资产/平均股东权益）＝ROA×财务杠杆。三因素：ROE＝（净利润/营业收入）×（营业收入/平均总资产）×（平均总资产/平均权益）＝净利率×总资产周转率×财务杠杆。

Front:
Five-way DuPont decomposition
五因素杜邦分解
Back:
ROE = (Net income / EBT) × (EBT / EBIT) × (EBIT / Revenue) × (Revenue / Average TA) × (Average TA / Average equity) = Tax burden × Interest burden × EBIT margin × Total asset turnover × Financial leverage. Tax burden = 1 minus average tax rate (proportion of pretax profit kept). Interest burden captures interest expense effect (rising interest lowers EBT/EBIT and ROE). EBIT margin captures operating profitability.
ROE＝（净利润/EBT）×（EBT/EBIT）×（EBIT/收入）×（收入/平均总资产）×（平均总资产/平均权益）＝税负比率×利息负担比率×EBIT 利润率×总资产周转率×财务杠杆。税负比率＝1−平均税率（税前利润中留存的比例）；利息负担比率反映利息费用的影响（利息上升会降低 EBT/EBIT 及 ROE）；EBIT 利润率反映经营盈利能力。

Front:
Equity valuation ratios (P/E, P/CF, P/S, P/BV)
股权估值比率（P/E、P/CF、P/S、P/BV）
Back:
P/E = Price per share / EPS; tells how much a share is worth per dollar of earnings. P/CF = Price per share / Cash flow per share; cash flow is less subject to manipulation than earnings, useful for comparing accounting aggressiveness. P/S = Price per share / Sales per share; sales are less distorted and it works when net income is negative. P/BV = Price per share / Book value per share; book value is more stable than EPS, so P/BV is more meaningful when EPS is abnormally high, low, or volatile.
P/E＝每股价格/每股收益，表示每 1 元盈利对应的股价；P/CF＝每股价格/每股现金流，现金流比利润更难被操纵，可用于比较会计处理的激进程度；P/S＝每股价格/每股销售额，销售额受扭曲较小，且在净利润为负时仍可使用；P/BV＝每股价格/每股账面价值，账面价值比每股收益更稳定，因此当每股收益异常偏高、偏低或波动剧烈时，P/BV 更有意义。

Front:
Basic EPS vs. diluted EPS
基本每股收益与稀释每股收益
Back:
Basic EPS = (Net income - Preferred dividends) / Weighted average number of common shares outstanding. Diluted EPS = Adjusted net income available to common / (Weighted average common shares + potential dilutive securities converted to common). Dilutive securities include convertible debt, convertible preferred stock, options, and warrants. Net income available to common is increased by after-tax interest savings on dilutive debt and by dividends on dilutive convertible preferred to get adjusted net income.
基本 EPS＝（净利润−优先股股利）/流通在外普通股加权平均数。稀释 EPS＝调整后可归属于普通股的净利润/（加权平均普通股数＋潜在稀释性证券转换的普通股数）。稀释性证券包括可转换债券、可转换优先股、期权和认股权证。计算调整时，需将稀释性可转换债券的税后利息和稀释性可转换优先股的股利加回净利润，得到调整后净利润。

Front:
Dividend payout, retention, and sustainable growth rate
股利支付率、留存率与可持续增长率
Back:
Dividend payout rate (DPR) = (Total dividends / Net income) × 100% (percentage of earnings paid as dividends). Retention rate = 1 - dividend payout rate (percentage of earnings retained). Sustainable growth rate (g) = retention rate × ROE = (1 - dividend payout rate) × ROE; it is a function of profitability (ROE) and the ability to self-finance from retained earnings.
股利支付率（DPR）＝（股利总额/净利润）×100%（利润中以股利形式支付的比例）；留存率＝1−股利支付率（利润中留存的比例）；可持续增长率（g）＝留存率×ROE＝（1−股利支付率）×ROE，它是盈利能力（ROE）与依靠留存收益自我融资能力的函数。

Front:
Coefficient of variation for business risk
衡量经营风险的变异系数
Back:
Business risk is measured by the coefficient of variation (standard deviation / average) of key items: coefficient of variation of operating income = SD of operating income / average operating income; of net income = SD of net income / average net income; and of revenues = SD of revenue / average revenue. Higher coefficients indicate greater business risk.
经营风险用关键项目的变异系数（标准差/平均值）衡量：营业利润变异系数＝营业利润标准差/平均营业利润；净利润变异系数＝净利润标准差/平均净利润；收入变异系数＝收入标准差/平均收入。变异系数越高，经营风险越大。

Front:
Financial sector (bank) ratios
金融行业（银行）比率
Back:
Capital adequacy ratio (CAR) = Various components of capital / risk-based measures (e.g., risk-weighted assets, market risk exposure). Monetary reserve requirement = Reserves held at central bank / Specified deposit liabilities. Liquid asset requirement = Approved readily marketable securities / Specified deposit liabilities. Net interest margin = Net interest income / Total interest-earning assets.
资本充足率（CAR）＝各类资本组成部分/基于风险的计量指标（如风险加权资产、市场风险敞口）；法定存款准备金要求＝存放于中央银行的准备金/规定的存款负债；流动资产要求＝经批准的易变现证券/规定的存款负债；净息差＝净利息收入/计息资产总额。

Front:
Credit analysis ratios
信用分析比率
Back:
Credit analysis evaluates credit risk (loss from a debtor's failure to pay). Ratios include: EBITDA interest coverage = EBITDA / Interest expense; FFO (funds from operations) to debt = FFO / Total debt; free operating cash flow to debt = [CFO (adjusted) - Capital expenditure] / Total debt; EBIT margin = EBIT / Total revenues; EBITDA margin = EBITDA / Total revenues; Debt to EBITDA = Total debt / EBITDA; Return on capital = EBIT / Average beginning- and end-of-year capital.
信用分析用于评估信用风险（债务人未能偿付造成的损失）。常用比率包括：EBITDA 利息保障倍数＝EBITDA/利息费用；营运资金（FFO）与债务之比＝FFO/总债务；自由经营现金流与债务之比＝〔经营现金流（调整后）−资本支出〕/总债务；EBIT 利润率＝EBIT/总收入；EBITDA 利润率＝EBITDA/总收入；债务与 EBITDA 之比＝总债务/EBITDA；资本回报率＝EBIT/年初与年末资本的平均值。

Front:
Business segment and geographic segment definitions
业务分部与地区分部的定义
Back:
A business segment is a portion of a company that accounts for more than 10% of revenue or assets and is distinguishable from other lines of business in terms of risk and return characteristics. A geographic segment meets the same criteria and operates in a business environment different from other segments or the rest of the company's business.
业务分部是指占公司收入或资产 10% 以上、且在风险与回报特征上可与其他业务相区分的组成部分。地区分部须满足相同标准，并在与其他分部或公司其余业务不同的经营环境中运作。

Front:
Segment ratios
分部比率
Back:
Segment margin = Segment profit (loss) / Segment revenue (operating profitability relative to sales). Segment turnover = Segment revenue / Segment assets (revenue generated per dollar of assets). Segment ROA = Segment profit (loss) / Segment assets (operating profitability relative to assets). Segment debt ratio = Segment liabilities / Segment assets (solvency of the segment).
分部利润率＝分部利润（亏损）/分部收入（相对于销售额的经营盈利能力）；分部周转率＝分部收入/分部资产（每单位资产创造的收入）；分部 ROA＝分部利润（亏损）/分部资产（相对于资产的经营盈利能力）；分部债务比率＝分部负债/分部资产（该分部的偿债能力）。

Front:
Techniques to model and forecast earnings
收益建模与预测技术
Back:
Sensitivity analysis shows the range of possible outcomes as underlying assumptions are altered (e.g., net income if more debt is issued). Scenario analysis shows changes in key financial quantities from given economic events, such as loss of customers, loss of a supply source, or a catastrophic event. Monte Carlo simulation is computer-generated sensitivity or scenario analysis based on probability models, assigning a probability to each outcome and running multiple scenarios.
敏感性分析展示了当基本假设发生变化时可能结果的范围（例如，如果发行更多债务，净收入会如何变化）。情景分析显示了给定经济事件（如客户流失、供应源丧失或灾难性事件）导致的关键财务数量的变化。蒙特卡洛模拟是基于概率模型的计算机生成敏感性或情景分析，为每个结果分配一个概率并运行多个情景。

Front:
Four Cs of credit analysis
信用分析的 4C 原则
Back:
Credit analysis evaluates the four Cs: Character refers to the quality of management; Capacity refers to the ability of the issuer to fulfill its obligations; Collateral refers to the assets pledged to secure a loan; and Covenants are limitations and restrictions on the activities of issuers.
信用分析评估四个 C：品德（Character）指管理层的素质；能力（Capacity）指发行人履行债务义务的能力；抵押品（Collateral）指为担保贷款而抵押的资产；契约（Covenants）指对发行人行为的限制与约束。

Front:
Credit rating agency considerations
信用评级机构的考量因素
Back:
Rating agencies (Moody's, S&P) use weighted averages of accounting ratios and business characteristics. Items considered: scale and diversification (larger companies have leverage in negotiations, implying lower credit risk); operational efficiency (higher return on assets implies lower credit risk); margin stability (high profit margins imply higher probability of repayment, so lower credit risk); and leverage (high ratios of free cash flow to total debt and to interest expense imply lower credit risk).
评级机构（穆迪、标普）使用会计比率和业务特征的加权平均。考量因素包括：规模与多元化（大公司在谈判中更有优势，意味着信用风险较低）；经营效率（资产收益率越高，信用风险越低）；利润率稳定性（高利润率意味着偿债概率更高，信用风险较低）；杠杆水平（自由现金流与总债务之比、自由现金流与利息费用之比越高，信用风险越低）。

Front:
Screening for equity investments: top-down vs. bottom-up
股票投资筛选：自上而下与自下而上
Back:
Screening filters a set of potential investments into a smaller set with desirable characteristics by applying criteria. Top-down analysis identifies attractive geographical and industry segments, then chooses the most attractive investments within them. Bottom-up analysis selects specific investments within a specific investment universe. Screens are used by growth investors (high earnings-growth firms), value investors (low price relative to earnings/assets), and market-oriented investors.
筛选是通过设定标准，将一组潜在投资缩小为具有理想特征的较小集合。自上而下分析先识别有吸引力的地区和行业板块，再在其中选择最具吸引力的投资标的；自下而上分析则在特定投资范围内直接挑选具体标的。成长型投资者（高盈利增长公司）、价值型投资者（价格相对盈利/资产偏低）以及市场导向型投资者都会使用筛选。

Front:
Backtesting biases
回测偏差
Back:
Backtesting screens historical data to see how portfolios based on criteria would have performed. Survivorship bias: if the database eliminates companies that ceased to exist (merger/bankruptcy), the remaining companies appear to have performed better. Look-ahead bias: if data is updated for restatements, there is a mismatch between what investors actually knew at the time and the information used in backtesting. Data-snooping bias: building models on prior researchers' findings and testing on the same database is not a true test.
回测是用历史数据检验基于特定标准构建的投资组合会取得怎样的表现。幸存者偏差：若数据库剔除了已消失的公司（并购/破产），留存公司会显得表现更好。前视偏差：若数据按重述后的版本更新，投资者当时实际掌握的信息与回测所用信息之间会出现错配。数据挖掘偏差：基于前人研究结论建模、并在同一数据库上检验，并非真正的检验。

Front:
Analyst adjustments: inventory (LIFO) and investments
分析师调整：存货（LIFO）与投资
Back:
When companies use different methods, statements become incomparable and analysts must adjust. Inventory: a firm using LIFO reports higher COGS, lower income, and lower inventory when costs are rising; adjust LIFO COGS and inventory to FIFO-equivalent values using the LIFO reserve. Investments: securities classified as held-for-trading, available-for-sale, or held-to-maturity cause significant differences in reported net income or balance sheet asset values, so adjust net income and assets.
当公司使用不同会计方法时，报表失去可比性，分析师必须进行调整。存货：成本上升时，采用 LIFO 的公司报告的销货成本更高、利润更低、存货更低；应利用 LIFO 储备将 LIFO 下的销货成本和存货调整为 FIFO 等值口径。投资：划分为交易性、可供出售或持有至到期的证券会导致报告的净利润或资产负债表资产价值出现重大差异，因此需相应调整净利润和资产。

Front:
Analyst adjustments: PP&E and goodwill
分析师调整：固定资产与商誉
Back:
PP&E: differences in depreciation methods, useful lives, and salvage values cause significant differences in income and asset values. Gross fixed assets = Accumulated depreciation + Net fixed assets; estimated useful life = Gross fixed assets / Annual depreciation; average age = Accumulated depreciation / Annual depreciation; remaining life = Net fixed assets / Annual depreciation. Goodwill: subtract goodwill from assets when calculating ratios and rely on price-to-tangible-book value; reverse any goodwill impairment expense in the current period, increasing reported net income.
固定资产：折旧方法、使用年限和残值的差异会导致利润和资产价值出现重大差异。固定资产原值＝累计折旧＋固定资产净值；估计使用年限＝固定资产原值/年折旧额；平均已用年限＝累计折旧/年折旧额；剩余使用年限＝固定资产净值/年折旧额。商誉：计算比率时从资产中剔除商誉，并改用股价/有形资产账面价值比率；转回当期确认的商誉减值费用，从而提高报告的净利润。

Front:
Financial statement analysis framework — the six steps
财务报表分析框架——六个步骤
Back:
The generic FSA framework has six steps: 1) Articulate the purpose and context of the analysis; 2) Collect input data; 3) Process data; 4) Analyze/interpret the processed data; 5) Develop and communicate conclusions and recommendations; 6) Follow-up.
通用财务报表分析框架包括六个步骤：（1）阐明分析的目的与背景；（2）收集输入数据；（3）加工处理数据；（4）分析并解读加工后的数据；（5）形成并传达结论与建议；（6）跟踪后续。

Front:
Step 1: Articulate purpose and context
步骤 1：阐明目的与背景
Back:
Defining the analyst's function (e.g., evaluating an equity or debt investment, issuing a credit rating), communicating with the client or supervisor on needs and concerns, following institutional guidelines, stating the purpose/objective, listing specific questions to answer, and setting the report content, timetable, and budget.
界定分析师的职能（如评估股权或债权投资、出具信用评级）；与客户或主管沟通其需求与关注点；遵循机构指引；阐明目的/目标；列出需要回答的具体问题；并确定报告内容、时间表与预算。

Front:
Step 4 vs Step 6 outputs in the FSA framework
FSA 框架中步骤 4 与步骤 6 的产出
Back:
Step 4 (Analyze/interpret) produces an analytical report answering the questions posed in Phase 1 plus a recommendation regarding the purpose (e.g., whether to invest or grant credit). Step 6 (Follow-up) produces updated reports and recommendations.
步骤 4（分析/解读）产出分析报告，回答第一阶段提出的问题，并就分析目的给出建议（如是否投资、是否授信）；步骤 6（跟踪）产出更新后的报告与建议。

Front:
Role of financial reporting vs role of financial statement analysis
财务报告的作用与财务报表分析的作用
Back:
Financial reporting is the way companies show their financial performance to investors, creditors, and other parties by preparing and presenting financial statements. Financial statement analysis uses the information in those statements, along with other relevant information, to make economic decisions — evaluating past performance and current position to form opinions about future profits and cash flows.
财务报告是公司通过编制和列报财务报表，向投资者、债权人及其他相关方展示其财务业绩的方式；财务报表分析则是利用这些报表中的信息及其他相关信息做出经济决策——评估过去的业绩与当前的财务状况，从而形成对未来利润和现金流的判断。

Front:
The four financial statements (plus notes)
四张财务报表（加附注）
Back:
A complete set comprises: 1) Statement of financial position (balance sheet); 2) Statement of comprehensive income (income statement); 3) Statement of cash flows; 4) Statement of changes in equity. The accompanying required notes/footnotes are an integral part of a complete set.
完整的一套报表包括：（1）财务状况表（资产负债表）；（2）综合收益表（利润表）；（3）现金流量表；（4）所有者权益变动表。附带的必备附注/脚注是完整报表不可分割的组成部分。

Front:
Statement of financial position — role and basic equation
财务状况表——作用与基本等式
Back:
Reports major classes and amounts of assets (resources owned or controlled), liabilities (external claims on those assets), and stockholders' equity (owners' contributions and internally generated capital) at a specific point in time. Basic equation: Total assets = Total liabilities + Equity.
在特定时点报告资产（拥有或控制的资源）、负债（对该等资产的外部索取权）和股东权益（所有者出资及内部积累的资本）的主要类别与金额。基本等式：总资产＝总负债＋股东权益。

Front:
Statement of comprehensive income — equations
综合收益表——等式
Back:
Reports firm performance from revenues, expenses, gains and losses in a period. Total comprehensive income = Net income + Other comprehensive income (OCI). Net income = Revenues − Expenses. The P&L (income statement) contains realized income/expense; OCI contains unrealized income/expense. It can be presented as a single statement or as two statements (income statement plus statement of comprehensive income).
报告公司在某一期间内由收入、费用、利得和损失反映的经营业绩。综合收益总额＝净利润＋其他综合收益（OCI）；净利润＝收入−费用。利润表包含已实现的收入/费用，OCI 包含未实现的收入/费用。可以采用单一报表列报，也可以分为两张报表（利润表＋综合收益表）。

Front:
Examples of items reported in Other Comprehensive Income (OCI)
计入其他综合收益（OCI）的项目示例
Back:
OCI holds unrealized items such as unrealized gains/losses on available-for-sale (FVOCI) debt securities, unrealized gains/losses on available-for-sale equity securities, and foreign currency translation adjustments.
OCI 核算未实现项目，如可供出售（FVOCI）债务证券的未实现损益、可供出售权益证券的未实现损益，以及外币折算调整。

Front:
Statement of cash flows — three classifications and equation
现金流量表——三大分类与等式
Back:
Reports cash receipts and payments classified as: Operating CF (cash from normal business activities); Investing CF (cash from acquisition/sale of PP&E, a subsidiary or segment, investments in other firms); Financing CF (cash from issuance/retirement of debt and equity securities and dividends paid). Net cash in SOCF = Net operating CF + Net investing CF + Net financing CF.
报告现金收支，分为：经营活动现金流（正常经营活动产生的现金）；投资活动现金流（购建/处置固定资产、子公司或分部以及投资其他企业的现金）；筹资活动现金流（发行/偿付债务和权益证券及支付股利的现金）。现金流量表净现金＝经营活动净现金流＋投资活动净现金流＋筹资活动净现金流。

Front:
Profit versus cash flow (accrual timing)
利润与现金流（权责发生制的时间差异）
Back:
Profit and cash flow can differ in a period because of timing. In the Sennett Designs example, December profit was €80,000 (sales €250,000 − COGS €150,000 − rent/salaries €20,000) but December cash flow was €230,000 because the €150,000 for goods bought on credit was not paid until January. In January, profit stayed €80,000 and cash flow was also €80,000 once the prior purchase was paid. Over time, total profit equals total cash flow, but timing differs.
由于确认时点不同，利润与现金流在同一期间可能不同。在 Sennett Designs 的例子中，12 月利润为 80,000 欧元（销售 250,000−销货成本 150,000−租金/工资 20,000），但 12 月现金流为 230,000 欧元，因为赊购货物的 150,000 欧元直到 1 月才支付。1 月利润仍为 80,000 欧元，支付该笔购货款后现金流也是 80,000 欧元。长期来看，利润总额等于现金流总额，但确认时点不同。

Front:
Statement of changes in equity — role and equation
所有者权益变动表——作用与等式
Back:
Reports movements (increases and decreases) in the components of owners' equity over a period, including changes in retained earnings, share capital reserves, and subscribed capital. Basic equation: Closing equity = Opening equity + Movement in equity. Typical columns include share capital, share premium, retained earnings, revaluation surplus, and unrealized gains on FVOCI investments.
报告某一期间所有者权益各组成部分的增减变动，包括留存收益、股本溢价储备和认缴资本的变化。基本等式：期末权益＝期初权益＋权益变动额。典型栏目包括股本、股本溢价、留存收益、重估盈余以及 FVOCI 投资的未实现收益。

Front:
IOSCO and the US SEC
国际证监会组织（IOSCO）与美国证监会（SEC）
Back:
IOSCO (International Organization of Securities Commissions) is recognized as the global standard setter for the securities sector; its core objectives are protecting investors, ensuring markets are fair/efficient/transparent, and reducing systemic risk. The US SEC has primary responsibility for US securities and capital markets regulation and is an ordinary member of IOSCO; any company issuing securities in the US (e.g., NYSE, NASDAQ) is subject to SEC rules.
IOSCO 被公认为证券行业的全球标准制定者，其核心目标是保护投资者、确保市场公平/高效/透明并降低系统性风险。美国 SEC 对美国证券与资本市场监管负有首要责任，是 IOSCO 的普通成员；任何在美国发行证券的公司（如在纽交所 NYSE、纳斯达克 NASDAQ 上市）均须遵守 SEC 规则。

Front:
Importance of financial statement notes (footnotes)
财务报表附注（脚注）的重要性
Back:
Notes are essential to understanding the primary statements. They discuss the basis of presentation (fiscal period, consolidated entities); provide information on accounting methods, assumptions, and estimates used by management; and give additional detail on items such as business acquisitions/disposals, legal actions, employee benefit plans, contingencies and commitments, significant customers, related-party transactions, and business segments.
附注对理解主表至关重要：说明列报基础（会计期间、合并主体范围）；提供管理层所采用会计方法、假设和估计的信息；并对业务收购/处置、法律诉讼、员工福利计划、或有事项与承诺、重要客户、关联方交易和业务分部等事项提供进一步细节。

Front:
Operating segment — definition and disclosure
经营分部——定义与披露
Back:
An operating segment is a component that engages in activities that may generate revenue and create expenses (including a start-up segment yet to earn revenue), whose results are regularly reviewed by senior management, and for which discrete financial information is available. Both IFRS and US GAAP require some disaggregated segment information in the notes.
经营分部是指从事可能产生收入并发生费用的活动的组成部分（包括尚未产生收入的初创分部），其经营成果由高级管理层定期审阅，且可获得独立的财务信息。IFRS 与美国 GAAP 均要求在附注中披露一定的分部细分信息。

Front:
Management's commentary (MD&A) — content and caution
管理层讨论与分析（MD&A）——内容与注意事项
Back:
Management's commentary (required under US GAAP), also called MD&A or operating & financial review, highlights trends and events affecting liquidity, capital resources, and operations; discusses prospects (inflation, goals, material events, uncertainties); and must discuss critical accounting policies requiring subjective judgment with material impact. Important caution: the MD&A section is not audited.
管理层评论（美国 GAAP 要求），亦称 MD&A 或经营与财务回顾，重点说明影响流动性、资本资源和经营的趋势与事件；讨论前景（通胀、目标、重大事件、不确定性）；并须讨论需要主观判断且具有重大影响的关键会计政策。重要提示：MD&A 部分未经审计。

Front:
Objectives of an audit of financial statements
财务报表审计的目标
Back:
An audit is an independent review of an entity's financial statements. Its objectives are: obtain reasonable assurance that the statements as a whole are free from material misstatement; give an opinion on the accounting standards, estimates, and assumptions applied; give an opinion on the internal control system (only required under GAAP); and report on the statements in accordance with the ISAs. Materiality: information is material if its omission or misstatement could influence users' decisions.
审计是对主体财务报表的独立审查，其目标是：就报表整体是否不存在重大错报获取合理保证；对所采用的会计准则、估计和假设发表意见；对内部控制制度发表意见（仅美国 GAAP 要求）；并按照《国际审计准则》（ISA）对财务报表作出报告。重要性：若信息的遗漏或错报可能影响使用者的决策，则该信息是重要的。

Front:
Four types of audit opinion
四种审计意见
Back:
Unqualified (clean): financial statements are free from material omissions and errors — the preferred opinion. Qualified: there is a scope limitation or an exception to standards. Adverse: the statements materially depart from accounting standards. Disclaimer: the auditor is unable to issue an opinion. For listed companies the report also contains Key Audit Matters (international) or Critical Audit Matters (US).
无保留意见（清洁意见）：财务报表不存在重大遗漏和错误，是最理想的意见；保留意见：存在审计范围受限或偏离准则的例外事项；否定意见：报表在重大方面偏离会计准则；无法表示意见：审计师无法发表意见。上市公司的审计报告还包含关键审计事项（国际准则称 KAM，美国称 CAM）。

Front:
Internal control system — purpose and US requirements
内部控制制度——目的与美国要求
Back:
The internal control system is the company's internal system designed to ensure its process for generating financial reports is sound. It reduces the risk of asset loss and helps ensure information is complete and accurate, statements are reliable, and operations comply with applicable laws. US companies must explicitly accept responsibility for the effectiveness of internal control, evaluate it using suitable control criteria, and provide a report on internal control.
内部控制制度是公司内部旨在确保财务报告生成流程健全的制度。它降低资产损失风险，有助于确保信息完整准确、报表可靠、经营符合适用法律。美国公司必须明确承担内部控制有效性的责任，采用适当的控制标准进行评估，并出具内部控制报告。

Front:
Annual vs interim financial reports
年度报告与中期报告
Back:
An annual report provides unaudited financial statements published by the company annually. An interim report provides unaudited financial statements published semi-annually or quarterly. (Note: the module labels both as unaudited.)
年度报告是公司每年发布的财务报表（本模块将其标注为未经审计）；中期报告是每半年或每季度发布的未经审计财务报表。（注：本模块将两者均标注为未经审计。）

Front:
Other information sources besides annual/interim reports
除年度/中期报告外的其他信息来源
Back:
Beyond annual and interim reports and notes, analysts use: issuer sources (earnings calls, presentations and events, press releases, company website, speaking with management/investor relations); public third-party sources (economic/industry indicators, general and industry-specific news, social media, analyst reports); proprietary third-party sources (reports/data from platforms and consultancies); and proprietary primary research (surveys, conversations, product comparisons, and commissioned studies).
除年度、中期报告及附注外，分析师还使用：发行人来源（业绩电话会、推介会与活动、新闻稿、公司网站、与管理层/投资者关系部门沟通）；公开第三方来源（经济/行业指标、综合及行业新闻、社交媒体、分析师报告）；付费第三方来源（数据平台与咨询机构的报告/数据）；以及专有的一手研究（问卷调查、访谈、产品对比和委托研究）。

Front:
Earnings calls (information source)
业绩电话会（信息来源）
Back:
Earnings calls are webcast or teleconferenced presentations and question-and-answer sessions hosted by issuers' management to discuss financial results. Presentations and events are similar but scheduled on an ad hoc basis, where management gives in-depth presentations on the business or specific segments.
业绩电话会是发行人管理层为讨论财务业绩而主持的网络直播或电话会议及问答环节。推介会和活动类似，但属不定期安排，管理层在会上就业务或特定分部作深入介绍。

Front:
Major differences between US GAAP and IFRS
美国 GAAP 与 IFRS 的主要差异
Back:
US GAAP is developed by the FASB and is rules-based; IFRS is developed by the IASB and is principles-based. Interest paid: US GAAP classifies it as CFO, IFRS allows CFO or CFF. Inventory valuation: US GAAP permits FIFO, LIFO, and weighted average; IFRS permits FIFO and weighted average (no LIFO). Development cost: expensed under US GAAP, capitalized under IFRS if certain conditions are met. Inventory write-down reversal: prohibited under US GAAP, permissible under IFRS if conditions are met.
美国 GAAP 由 FASB 制定，以规则为基础；IFRS 由 IASB 制定，以原则为基础。已付利息：美国 GAAP 归类为经营现金流（CFO），IFRS 允许归入经营或筹资现金流（CFF）。存货计价：美国 GAAP 允许 FIFO、LIFO 和加权平均法；IFRS 仅允许 FIFO 和加权平均法（不允许 LIFO）。开发支出：美国 GAAP 予以费用化，IFRS 在符合特定条件时予以资本化。存货跌价转回：美国 GAAP 禁止，IFRS 在符合条件时允许。

Front:
Implications of alternative reporting systems for analysis
不同报告准则对分析的影响
Back:
Because reconciliation disclosures between IFRS and US GAAP are not required, an analyst comparing two companies using different standards must be aware of areas where standards have not converged. The analyst must maintain caution in interpreting comparative financial measures produced under different standards and monitor significant developments in financial reporting standards.
由于 IFRS 与美国 GAAP 之间的调节披露并非强制要求，分析师在比较采用不同准则的两家公司时，必须了解准则尚未趋同的领域；必须谨慎解读按不同准则编制的可比财务指标，并持续关注财务报告准则的重大发展。

Front:
Monitoring developments in reporting standards; role of CFA Institute
跟踪报告准则的发展；CFA 协会的作用
Back:
New products or transaction types arise from economic events (e.g., fintech), newly developed instruments/structures (e.g., cryptocurrencies and digital assets), or purposes such as window dressing rather than risk mitigation. When a new standard is proposed, an exposure draft is made available and users (e.g., CFA Institute) can draft comment letters and position papers for submission to the IASB and FASB to evaluate the proposal.
新产品或交易类型源于经济事件（如金融科技）、新开发的工具/结构（如加密货币与数字资产），或出于粉饰报表而非缓释风险等目的。新准则提出时会发布征求意见稿，使用者（如 CFA 协会）可起草意见函和立场文件提交 IASB 和 FASB，以评估该提案。

Front:
Objective of financial reporting
财务报告的目标
Back:
Financial reporting requires policy choices and estimates that need judgment varying from preparer to preparer, so standards are needed for consistency. The objective is to provide financial information useful to users in: making decisions about providing resources to the entity (relating to equity and debt instruments, or loans/credit — i.e., buying, selling, or holding), and influencing management's actions that affect the use of the entity's economic resources.
财务报告需要政策选择与估计，不同编制者的判断各不相同，因此需要准则以保持一致性。其目标是提供对使用者有用的财务信息，帮助其：就向主体提供资源作出决策（涉及权益与债务工具或贷款/授信，即买入、卖出或持有）；并影响管理层涉及主体经济资源运用的行为。

Front:
Standard-setting bodies vs regulatory authorities
准则制定机构与监管机构
Back:
Financial reporting standard-setting bodies are private-sector organizations of accountants and auditors that develop reporting rules and accounting standards (e.g., IASB issues IFRS; FASB issues US GAAP). Regulatory authorities are governmental entities with legal authority to enforce the reporting requirements set by the standard-setting bodies (e.g., SEC in the US; FSA in the UK). IOSCO is not a regulatory authority, but its members regulate much of the world's capital markets.
财务报告准则制定机构是由会计师和审计师组成的私营部门组织，负责制定报告规则和会计准则（如 IASB 发布 IFRS，FASB 发布美国 GAAP）。监管机构是拥有法律权力、可强制执行准则制定机构所定报告要求的政府部门（如美国 SEC、英国 FSA）。IOSCO 并非监管机构，但其成员监管着全球大部分资本市场。

Front:
Objectives of the IASB
IASB 的目标
Back:
The IASB is the independent standard-setting body of the IFRS Foundation. Its objectives are to develop and promote the use and adoption of a single set of high-quality financial standards; ensure the standards yield transparent, comparable, and decision-useful information while considering the needs of diverse entity sizes/types and economic settings; and promote the convergence of national accounting standards and IFRS. The FASB's objective is to improve financial reporting standards so information is useful for decision-making.
IASB 是 IFRS 基金会下属的独立准则制定机构，其目标是：制定并推广采用一套高质量的财务报告准则；在兼顾不同规模/类型主体及不同经济环境需求的同时，确保准则产生透明、可比且有助于决策的信息；推动各国会计准则与 IFRS 趋同。FASB 的目标是改进财务报告准则，使信息有助于决策。

Front:
IASB Conceptual Framework — three components
IASB 概念框架——三个组成部分
Back:
The Conceptual Framework consists of three components: qualitative characteristics of financial statements; constraints on financial statements; and reporting elements of financial statements.
概念框架由三部分组成：财务报表的质量特征；财务报表的约束条件；财务报表的报告要素。

Front:
Fundamental qualitative characteristics: relevance and faithful representation
基本质量特征：相关性与如实反映
Back:
The two fundamental characteristics that make information useful are relevance and faithful representation. Relevance includes confirmatory value (useful to evaluate past decisions/forecasts), predictive value (useful in making forecasts), and materiality. Faithful representation means information is complete (all necessary information depicted), neutral (presented without bias), and free from error (no errors or omissions in description or in producing the information).
使信息有用的两个基本特征是相关性和如实反映。相关性包括确证价值（有助于评价过去的决策/预测）、预测价值（有助于作出预测）和重要性。如实反映意味着信息完整（描绘所有必要信息）、中立（无偏见地呈现）且无差错（描述或生成信息过程中无错误或遗漏）。

Front:
Enhancing qualitative characteristics
提升性质量特征
Back:
Four enhancing characteristics improve usefulness: comparability (presentation is consistent among firms and across time periods); verifiability (independent observers using the same methods obtain similar results); timeliness (information is available to decision-makers in time to influence decisions); and understandability (users with basic business and accounting knowledge can readily understand it, without omitting useful information).
四项提升性特征增强信息的有用性：可比性（不同公司之间及不同期间之间列报一致）；可验证性（独立观察者采用相同方法可得出类似结果）；及时性（信息能及时送达决策者以影响决策）；可理解性（具备基本商业和会计知识的使用者即可理解，且不得为此省略有用信息）。

Front:
Constraints on financial statements
财务报表的约束条件
Back:
Two constraints: benefit versus cost (does the cost of providing financial information exceed the benefits derived from it?); and omission of non-quantifiable information (intangible aspects such as company reputation, brand name, customer loyalty, and corporate culture cannot be quantified and reflected in financial statements).
两项约束：成本效益权衡（提供财务信息的成本是否超过其带来的收益？）；不可量化信息的省略（公司声誉、品牌、客户忠诚度、企业文化等无形方面无法量化并反映在财务报表中）。

Front:
Elements of the balance sheet: asset, liability, equity
资产负债表要素：资产、负债、权益
Back:
Asset: a resource controlled by the entity as a result of past events, from which future economic benefits arise. Liability: a present obligation of the entity arising from past events, to transfer an economic resource. Equity: the residual interest in the assets of the entity after deducting all its liabilities.
资产：主体因过去事项而控制、预期能带来未来经济利益的资源。负债：主体因过去事项而承担的、须转移经济资源的现时义务。权益：主体资产扣除全部负债后的剩余权益。

Front:
Elements of the income statement: income and expense
利润表要素：收益与费用
Back:
Income: an increase in economic benefits during the period, in the form of inflows (or enhancements) of assets or decreases of liabilities, resulting in an increase in equity (other than contributions from equity participants). Expense: a decrease in economic benefits during the period, in the form of outflows (or depletions) of assets or incurrences of liabilities, resulting in a decrease in equity (other than distributions to equity participants).
收益：本期经济利益的增加，表现为资产流入（或增值）或负债减少，从而导致权益增加（不含权益参与者的出资）。费用：本期经济利益的减少，表现为资产流出（或耗减）或负债的发生，从而导致权益减少（不含对权益参与者的分配）。

Front:
Underlying assumptions: accrual basis and going concern
基本假设：权责发生制与持续经营
Back:
Accrual basis: transactions are recorded when they actually occur, irrespective of when the related cash is exchanged; all activities are reported in the periods to which they relate. Going concern: the company will continue in operation for the foreseeable future, with no intention or need to liquidate; if such needs or intentions exist, the statements must be prepared on another basis.
权责发生制：交易在实际发生时确认，而不论相关现金何时收付；所有活动均在其所属期间报告。持续经营：公司将在可预见的未来持续经营，无清算的意图或必要；若存在此类意图或必要，报表须按其他基础编制。

Front:
Recognition of financial statement elements
财务报表要素的确认
Back:
Recognition means an item is included in the balance sheet or income statement. Recognition occurs if the item meets the definition of an element and satisfies the criteria for recognition. It is appropriate if it results in both relevant information about assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses and a faithful representation of those items, because the aim is to provide information useful to investors, lenders, and other creditors.
确认是指将某一项目纳入资产负债表或利润表。项目须符合要素定义并满足确认标准方可确认。当确认能同时提供有关资产、负债、权益、收入和费用的相关信息并如实反映这些项目时即为恰当，因为其目标是向投资者、贷款人及其他债权人提供有用信息。

Front:
Measurement bases: historical cost, current cost, amortized cost
计量基础：历史成本、现行成本、摊余成本
Back:
Historical cost — assets: cash/equivalents paid to purchase, including acquisition/preparation costs (or fair value of consideration given if not bought for cash); liabilities: proceeds received in exchange for the obligation. Current cost — assets: cash that would have to be paid to acquire the same asset currently; liabilities: undiscounted cash required to settle currently. Amortized cost: historical cost adjusted for amortization, depreciation, or depletion and/or impairment.
历史成本——资产：为购入支付的现金/现金等价物，包括购置及使资产达到预定用途的费用（若非以现金购买，则为所付对价的公允价值）；负债：承担义务所收取的对价。现行成本——资产：当前购置相同资产须支付的现金；负债：当前清偿所需支付的不贴现现金。摊余成本：经摊销、折旧或折耗及/或减值调整后的历史成本。

Front:
Measurement bases: realizable value, present value, fair value
计量基础：可变现价值、现值、公允价值
Back:
Realizable (settlement) value — assets: cash obtainable currently by selling the asset in an orderly disposal; liabilities: undiscounted cash expected to be paid to satisfy them in the normal course of business. Present value — assets: present discounted value of expected future cash inflows; liabilities: present discounted value of expected future net cash outflows to settle. Fair value: an exit price — the price to sell an asset or transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.
可变现（清偿）价值——资产：通过有序处置出售资产当前可获得的现金；负债：正常经营过程中预计为清偿债务而支付的不贴现现金。现值——资产：预期未来现金流入的贴现值；负债：清偿义务的预期未来净现金流出的贴现值。公允价值：脱手价格，即计量日市场参与者之间有序交易中出售资产或转移负债的价格。

Front:
IFRS general features for financial statements
IFRS 财务报表的一般特征
Back:
The general features required under IFRS are: fair presentation; going concern; accrual basis; materiality and aggregation (each material class of similar items presented separately; dissimilar items aggregated only if individually immaterial); no offsetting (assets/liabilities and income/expenses not offset unless required or permitted by IFRS); frequency of reporting (at least annually); comparative information (provided for the previous period); and consistency of presentation (retained period to period unless a change is justified).
IFRS 要求的一般特征包括：公允列报；持续经营；权责发生制；重要性与汇总（性质类似的项目中每个重要类别单独列报，不相似项目仅在个别不重要时才汇总）；不得抵销（除非 IFRS 要求或允许，资产/负债、收入/费用不得相互抵销）；报告频率（至少每年一次）；比较信息（提供上一期间数据）；列报一致性（除非有正当理由，各期间保持一致）。

Front:
IFRS structure and content requirements
IFRS 的结构与内容要求
Back:
IFRS structure/content requirements include: a classified balance sheet (distinguishing current from non-current assets and liabilities, unless a liquidity-based presentation is used, e.g., by banks); minimum specified information on the face of the statements (IAS 1 specifies minimum line items); minimum specified note disclosures (including accounting policies, sources of estimation uncertainty, and other disclosures such as entity description, parent name, and dividends not recognized); and comparative information.
IFRS 的结构/内容要求包括：分类列报的资产负债表（区分流动与非流动资产、负债，采用流动性列报的银行等除外）；报表列示的最低信息要求（IAS 1 规定了最低限度的列报行项目）；最低附注披露要求（包括会计政策、估计不确定性来源，以及主体描述、母公司名称、未确认股利等其他披露）；以及比较信息。

Front:
Required financial statements under IFRS
IFRS 要求的财务报表
Back:
IFRS requires: statement of financial position (balance sheet); statement of comprehensive income (a single statement, or an income statement plus a statement of comprehensive income); statement of changes in equity; statement of cash flows; notes; and, in certain cases, a balance sheet from the earliest comparative period.
IFRS 要求：财务状况表（资产负债表）；综合收益表（单一报表，或利润表加综合收益表）；所有者权益变动表；现金流量表；附注；以及在某些情况下提供最早比较期间的资产负债表。

Front:
Income statement: purpose and equation
利润表：目的与等式
Back:
The income statement presents the financial results of a company's activities over a period of time. The basic equation is: Net income = Revenue - Expenses. In expanded form: Net income = Revenue - Expenses in the ordinary activities + Other income - Other expenses + Gains - Losses.
利润表反映公司在一段期间内经营活动的财务成果。基本等式：净利润＝收入−费用。扩展形式：净利润＝收入−日常活动费用＋其他收益−其他费用＋利得−损失。

Front:
Revenue vs Net revenue
收入与净收入
Back:
Revenue generally refers to the amount charged for the delivery of goods or services in the ordinary activities of a business. Net revenue is total revenue adjusted for product returns and amounts unlikely to be collected: Net revenue = Revenue - Adjustments for returns and allowances.
收入一般指企业在日常活动中交付商品或提供服务所收取的金额。净收入是对销售退回及预计无法收回金额调整后的总收入：净收入＝收入−销售退回与折让调整。

Front:
Expenses (definition)
费用（定义）
Back:
Expenses reflect outflows, depletions of assets, and incurrences of liabilities in the course of the activities of a business. Expenses may be grouped and reported in different formats, subject to some specific requirements.
费用反映企业经营活动过程中的资产流出与耗减以及负债的发生。在满足特定要求的前提下，费用可按不同格式分类汇总列报。

Front:
Gross profit
毛利润
Back:
Gross profit is the revenue available after subtracting the costs of delivering goods or services: Gross profit = Net revenue - Cost of goods sold. For manufacturing/merchandising firms COGS is the cost of goods sold; for service firms it is the cost of services provided. When an income statement shows a gross profit subtotal it uses a multi-step format.
毛利润是扣除交付商品或服务成本后剩余的收入：毛利润＝净收入−销货成本。制造/商贸企业的销货成本（COGS）指已售商品成本；服务企业则指所提供服务的成本。利润表列示毛利润小计时，采用的是多步式格式。

Front:
Operating income (operating profit / EBIT)
营业利润（经营利润/EBIT）
Back:
Operating income is the profit from ordinary business activities before taxes and, for nonfinancial companies, before deducting interest expense: Operating income = Gross profit - Operating expenses. It is sometimes called EBIT (earnings before interest and taxes). For financial companies, interest expense is included in operating expenses because it relates to their operating activities.
营业利润是日常经营活动产生的、税前且（对非金融企业而言）未扣除利息费用的利润：营业利润＝毛利润−经营费用，有时称为 EBIT（息税前利润）。金融企业的利息费用与其经营活动相关，因此计入经营费用。

Front:
Multi-step vs single-step income statement format
多步式与单步式利润表格式
Back:
The format of the income statement is not specified and varies across companies. A multi-step format presents a gross profit subtotal (Revenue - COGS = Gross profit, then subtract operating expenses). A single-step format groups all revenues together and all expenses together without a separate gross profit line.
利润表格式未作强制规定，各公司不尽相同。多步式列示毛利润小计（收入−销货成本＝毛利润，再减去经营费用）；单步式将全部收入归为一组、全部费用归为一组，不单独列示毛利润。

Front:
Grouping expenses by nature vs by function
费用按性质分类与按功能分类
Back:
Expenses can be grouped by nature or by function. By nature: expenses are listed by type (e.g., purchases, changes in inventory, depreciation, rent, employee benefits) without combining them. By function (also called the cost of sales method): expenses are grouped by purpose, e.g., combining manufacturing and administration costs into categories like COGS.
费用可按性质或功能分类。按性质：费用按类型列示（如购货、存货变动、折旧、租金、员工福利），不予合并；按功能（亦称销售成本法）：费用按用途归集，如将制造与管理成本并入销货成本等类别。

Front:
Income: Revenue vs Gain
收益：收入与利得
Back:
Income is increases in economic benefits (inflows/enhancements of assets or decreases of liabilities) that increase equity, other than contributions from equity participants. Revenue arises from a company's ordinary business activities; a gain arises from secondary or peripheral activities (e.g., a restaurant selling surplus equipment above its carrying value is a gain, not revenue).
收益是经济利益增加（资产流入/增值或负债减少）并导致权益增加的部分，不含权益参与者的出资。收入来自公司日常经营活动；利得来自次要或外围活动（如餐厅以高于账面价值的价格出售闲置设备属于利得而非收入）。

Front:
General principle of revenue recognition (IFRS 15)
收入确认的一般原则（IFRS 15）
Back:
Under accrual accounting and IFRS 15, revenue is recognized when a performance obligation is satisfied by transferring a promised good or service to a customer (when the customer obtains control). Recognition can occur independently of cash movements: a credit sale creates accounts receivable at the time of sale, while payment in advance creates a liability (unearned revenue) recognized as revenue when goods are transferred.
在权责发生制和 IFRS 15 下，当企业通过向客户转让承诺的商品或服务履行履约义务（客户取得控制权）时确认收入。确认可独立于现金收付：赊销在销售时形成应收账款；预收款形成负债（预收收入/合同负债），在商品转让时才确认为收入。

Front:
Five-step revenue recognition model
收入确认五步法
Back:
The converged standard recognizes revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods/services in an amount reflecting the consideration the entity expects. The five steps are: (1) Identify the contract(s) with a customer; (2) Identify the separate/distinct performance obligations; (3) Determine the transaction price; (4) Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations; (5) Recognize revenue when (or as) the entity satisfies a performance obligation.
趋同后的准则要求以反映企业预期有权收取对价的金额确认收入，以描绘承诺商品/服务的转让。五个步骤：（1）识别与客户签订的合同；（2）识别合同中单独/可明确区分的履约义务；（3）确定交易价格；（4）将交易价格分摊至各履约义务；（5）在企业履行履约义务时（或随履约进度）确认收入。

Front:
Five contract criteria and 'probable' (IFRS vs US GAAP)
合同成立的五项标准及“很可能”（IFRS 与美国 GAAP）
Back:
A contract creates enforceable rights and obligations and must meet five criteria: all parties have approved and committed to perform; each party's rights are identifiable; payment terms are identifiable; the contract has commercial substance; and it is probable that consideration will be collected. 'Probable' differs: under IFRS it means more likely than not; under US GAAP it means likely to occur.
合同产生可执行的权利与义务，须满足五项标准：各方均已批准合同并承诺履行；各方权利可明确识别；付款条款可明确识别；合同具有商业实质；对价很可能收回。“很可能”的界定不同：IFRS 下指“发生的可能性大于不发生”；美国 GAAP 下指“很可能会发生”。

Front:
Distinct performance obligation
可明确区分的履约义务
Back:
A performance obligation is a promise to deliver a distinct good or service. A good/service is distinct if both: the customer can benefit from it on its own or with readily available resources, and the promise to transfer it can be identified separately from other promises. Each distinct performance obligation is accounted for separately; if not distinct, they are combined into a single performance obligation.
履约义务是交付可明确区分的商品或服务的承诺。商品/服务须同时满足两个条件方为可明确区分：客户能够从该商品/服务本身或结合易于获得的资源中受益；转让该商品/服务的承诺可与合同中其他承诺单独区分。每项可明确区分的履约义务单独核算；不可明确区分的则合并为单项履约义务。

Front:
Transaction price and its allocation
交易价格及其分摊
Back:
The transaction price is the amount the seller estimates it will receive in exchange for transferring the goods/services in the contract. The transaction price is allocated to each identified performance obligation based on the stand-alone selling price of each obligation. Example allocation: Revenue for a PO = Total price × (stand-alone price of PO / total stand-alone prices).
交易价格是卖方预计因转让合同约定的商品/服务而有权收取的对价金额。交易价格按各项履约义务的单独售价比例分摊至已识别的各项履约义务。分摊示例：某履约义务应确认的收入＝交易总价×（该履约义务单独售价/各履约义务单独售价之和）。

Front:
Recognizing revenue: factors indicating control
收入确认：表明控制权转移的因素
Back:
Revenue is recognized when the entity transfers control of the asset to the customer. Factors indicating the customer has obtained control at a point in time: the entity has a present right to payment; the customer has legal title; the customer has physical possession; the customer has the significant risks and rewards of ownership; and the customer has accepted the asset.
收入在企业将资产控制权转移给客户时确认。表明客户在某一时间点取得控制权的因素包括：企业拥有现时收款权；客户拥有法定所有权；客户实际占有该资产；客户承担所有权的重大风险并享有相应报酬；客户已验收该资产。

Front:
Long-term contract: percentage-of-completion (IFRS vs US GAAP)
长期合同：完工百分比法（IFRS 与美国 GAAP）
Back:
If a loss is expected on a contract, it is reported immediately under both standards. If the outcome can be reliably measured, both IFRS and US GAAP require the percentage-of-completion method, where percentage = actual cost / estimated total cost (or an engineering estimate). If the outcome cannot be reliably measured, IFRS reports revenue only to the extent of costs incurred, while US GAAP reports no revenue until the contract is finished (completed contract method).
若预计合同将发生亏损，两种准则下均须立即确认。若合同结果能够可靠计量，IFRS 与美国 GAAP 均要求采用完工百分比法，完工百分比＝已发生实际成本/预计总成本（或采用工程测算）。若结果无法可靠计量，IFRS 仅在已发生成本范围内确认收入，美国 GAAP 则在合同完工前不确认收入（全部完工法）。

Front:
Percentage-of-completion calculation (example)
完工百分比计算（示例）
Back:
Revenue recognized = Percentage of completion × total revenue, where Percentage of completion = cost incurred / total estimated cost. Example: a $10 million warehouse with $8 million estimated cost; $4 million incurred in year 1 gives 4/8 = 50% completion, so revenue = 50% × $10 = $5 million.
确认收入＝完工百分比×合同总收入，完工百分比＝已发生成本/预计总成本。示例：一座合同价 1,000 万美元、预计成本 800 万美元的仓库，第 1 年发生成本 400 万美元，完工百分比＝4/8＝50%，故确认收入＝50%×1,000 万＝500 万美元。

Front:
Variable consideration
可变对价
Back:
A performance bonus is added to revenue only if the condition to achieve the bonus is highly probable. Example: a $1 million bonus for completing a building in three years is excluded from the transaction price while completion is uncertain (year 1 revenue stays $5 million), but once completion becomes likely the bonus is included, making the price $11 million and cumulative revenue = 75% × $11 = $8.25 million.
只有当达成奖金条件的可能性极高时，绩效奖金才能计入收入。示例：三年内建成大楼可获 100 万美元奖金，在能否完工尚不确定时该奖金不计入交易价格（第 1 年收入仍为 500 万美元）；一旦完工变得很可能，奖金计入交易价格，总价变为 1,100 万美元，累计确认收入＝75%×1,100 万＝825 万美元。

Front:
Contract revisions
合同变更
Back:
A contract modification is treated as an extension of the existing contract if the goods/services to be provided are not distinct from those already transferred; it is treated as a new contract if they are distinct. In the extension case, costs and revenues are added to the existing contract and the percentage-of-completion is recomputed on the combined totals.
若拟提供的商品/服务与已转让的部分不可明确区分，合同变更视为原合同的延续；若可明确区分，则视为一项新合同。在延续情形下，成本与收入并入原合同，并基于合并后的总额重新计算完工百分比。

Front:
Acting as an agent vs principal
代理人与主要责任人
Back:
An agent (who is not responsible for providing the good/service and bears no inventory or credit risk) reports revenue equal to its commission only. A principal reports revenue equal to the gross amount of consideration and records the cost of the good/service as an expense. Example: a travel agent earning $1,000 commission on a $10,000 ticket reports $1,000 revenue as an agent.
代理人（不负责提供商品/服务，也不承担存货或信用风险）仅按佣金确认收入；主要责任人按对价总额确认收入，并将商品/服务成本确认为费用。示例：旅行社就一张 10,000 美元的机票赚取 1,000 美元佣金，作为代理人仅确认 1,000 美元收入。

Front:
Franchising and licensing revenue
特许经营与授权许可收入
Back:
A franchisor's revenue includes: company-owned store revenues; royalty fees (a percentage of the franchisee's sales, not total sales); upfront fees (recognized as deferred revenue and amortized to revenue on a straight-line basis); and supply chain revenues (food and equipment supplied to franchisees). Example: revenue = own store sales + royalty% × franchisee sales + upfront fee / term.
特许人的收入包括：直营店收入；特许权使用费（按被特许人销售额的一定比例，而非总销售额）；初始加盟费（确认为递延收入，在特许期内直线摊销计入收入）；供应链收入（向被特许人供应食品和设备）。示例：收入＝直营店销售额＋特许权使用费率×被特许人销售额＋初始加盟费/特许期限。

Front:
Software license vs Software as a Service (SaaS)
软件许可与软件即服务（SaaS）
Back:
A software license is recognized over the life of the contract if the supplier continues to update/enhance the software, customers are exposed to those updates, and updates do not transfer separate goods/services; otherwise (software 'sold as is') revenue is recognized at the time of license transfer. Software as a Service, where customers access software without taking physical possession, is always recognized over the life of the contract.
若供应商持续更新/增强软件、客户会接触到这些更新，且更新不构成单独转让的商品/服务，则软件许可收入在合同期内分期确认；否则（软件按“现状”出售），收入在许可转让时点确认。SaaS 模式下客户仅访问软件而不取得实物占有，收入一律在合同期内分期确认。

Front:
Bill-and-hold agreements
开票留置（Bill-and-hold）安排
Back:
In a bill-and-hold arrangement the customer pays for goods ahead of shipping. Revenue is treated as deferred but may be recorded before shipping if all criteria are met (per IFRS 15): the reason must be substantive; the goods are identified as belonging to the customer; the goods are complete and ready for transfer; and the goods cannot be redirected to another customer.
在开票留置安排中，客户在发货前付款。收入原则上递延确认，但满足以下全部条件时（依据 IFRS 15）可在发货前确认：该安排须有实质性理由；商品已被识别为属于客户；商品已完工并可随时交付；商品不得转用于其他客户。

Front:
General principle of expense recognition (matching)
费用确认的一般原则（配比原则）
Back:
Expenses are decreases in economic benefits (outflows/depletions of assets or incurrences of liabilities) that decrease equity, other than distributions to equity participants. Under the matching concept, expenses are matched with the revenue they generate (e.g., COGS). Period costs are expensed in the period incurred (e.g., administrative expenses). Some expenditures relating to future benefits are allocated systematically over time (e.g., depreciation).
费用是经济利益的减少（资产流出/耗减或负债发生），导致权益减少，不含对权益参与者的分配。在配比原则下，费用与其产生的收入相配比（如销货成本）；期间费用在发生当期计入损益（如管理费用）；与未来利益相关的部分支出则随时间系统分摊（如折旧）。

Front:
Inventory expense and COGS formula
存货费用与销货成本公式
Back:
Under the matching principle, COGS is matched against revenue when units are sold. Cost of goods sold = Opening inventory + Purchased inventory - Closing inventory. Example: selling 9,000 units costing $25 each gives COGS of $225,000 matched against revenue of $270,000 (9,000 × $30).
按配比原则，销货成本在商品售出时与收入配比。销货成本＝期初存货＋本期购入存货−期末存货。示例：售出 9,000 件、单位成本 25 美元，则销货成本 225,000 美元，与收入 270,000 美元（9,000×30 美元）相配比。

Front:
Inventory costing methods (FIFO, LIFO, WAC, specific identification)
存货计价方法（FIFO、LIFO、加权平均、个别认定）
Back:
FIFO: cost of earliest items purchased flows to COGS first, so ending inventory reflects the most recent purchases. LIFO: cost of the most recent items flows to COGS first, so ending inventory reflects the earliest purchases. Weighted average cost (WAC): averages total costs over total units available for both COGS and ending inventory. Specific identification: the actual price of each unit is used.
先进先出法（FIFO）：最早购入的商品先计入销货成本，期末存货反映最近购货；后进先出法（LIFO）：最近购入的商品先计入销货成本，期末存货反映最早购货；加权平均法（WAC）：将总成本在可供销售总量上平均，同时用于销货成本和期末存货；个别认定法：按每件商品的实际成本计价。

Front:
Uncollectible accounts (doubtful expense)
坏账（坏账费用）
Back:
Uncollectible accounts are amounts owed by customers who cannot or will not pay. Under the matching principle, a company estimates doubtful expense from its sales and records it as an expense (not a direct reduction of revenue), debiting doubtful expense and crediting the allowance for doubtful accounts. Doubtful expenses are generally classified as a selling and general administrative expense. The direct write-off method instead waits until a customer actually defaults to recognize the loss.
坏账是客户无力或不愿支付的欠款。按配比原则，公司根据销售额估计坏账费用并将其确认为费用（而非直接冲减收入），借记坏账费用、贷记坏账准备；坏账费用通常归入销售及管理费用。直接转销法则等到客户实际违约时才确认损失。

Front:
Warranty expense
保修费用
Back:
Warranty expense relates to costs of repairing or replacing products sold if they prove deficient under the terms of the warranty. Under the matching principle, a company estimates future warranty expenses, recognizes an estimated warranty expense in the period of the sale, and updates the expense based on experience over the life of the warranty.
保修费用是产品售出后若被证明不符合保修条款而发生的修理或更换成本。按配比原则，公司估计未来保修支出，在销售当期确认估计的保修费用，并在保修期内根据实际经验更新估计。

Front:
Depreciation and amortization
折旧与摊销
Back:
Depreciation/amortization is the process of systematically allocating the cost of long-lived assets over the period during which the assets are expected to provide economic benefits. Depreciation is the term commonly applied to tangible assets; amortization is applied to intangible assets. Measurement methods include straight-line, units-of-production, and accelerated methods.
折旧/摊销是将长期资产成本在其预期带来经济利益的期间内系统分摊的过程。折旧通常用于有形资产，摊销用于无形资产。计量方法包括直线法、产量法和加速折旧法。

Front:
Implications of expense recognition for analysis
费用确认对分析的影响
Back:
Because expense recognition requires estimates, firms can delay or accelerate expense recognition. Delayed expense recognition increases current net income and is therefore more aggressive. Analysts should consider the underlying reasons for a change in an expense estimate (e.g., did bad debt expense drop due to better collections or to manipulate income?) and compare a firm's estimates to industry peers (e.g., is a low warranty expense due to quality or aggressive recognition?).
由于费用确认依赖估计，公司可以推迟或提前确认费用。推迟确认费用会抬高当期净利润，因此更为激进。分析师应探究费用估计变动背后的原因（如坏账费用下降是收款改善还是利润操纵所致），并将公司的估计与同业比较（如保修费用偏低是源于产品质量还是激进确认？）。

Front:
Non-recurring items: reporting treatment table
非经常性项目：列报处理汇总
Back:
Unusual or infrequent items are presented as a separate component of income from continuing operations and recorded gross of tax. Discontinued operations are presented as a separate component after income from continuing operations and recorded net of tax. A change in accounting policy requires restating the prior-year income statement; a change in accounting estimate does not restate prior-year statements.
异常或偶发项目作为持续经营利润的单独组成部分列报，按税前金额记录；终止经营作为持续经营利润之后的单独组成部分列报，按税后净额记录。会计政策变更须重述上年度利润表；会计估计变更无须重述以前年度报表。

Front:
Unusual or infrequent items
异常或偶发项目
Back:
These are events that are either unusual in nature or infrequent in occurrence, such as gains/losses from selling assets or part of a business outside ordinary operations, and impairments, write-offs, write-downs, and restructuring costs. They are included in income from continuing operations and reported before tax. Analytically, review whether they should be included when forecasting future earnings, since some firms report 'unusual' losses nearly every year.
指性质异常或发生频率低的事项，如处置日常经营之外的资产或部分业务产生的损益，以及减值、核销、减记和重组成本。此类项目计入持续经营利润，按税前口径列报。分析时应审视在预测未来盈利时是否应将其纳入，因为有些公司几乎年年报告“异常”损失。

Front:
Discontinued operations
终止经营
Back:
A discontinued operation is one that management has decided to dispose of but has not yet done so, or has disposed of in the current year after it generated income or losses. To qualify, the assets, results of operations, and investing/financing activities of the segment must be separable from the company. Gains from disposal do not contribute to future income/cash flows and can be reported only after disposal (when realized). Analysts may exclude them when forecasting earnings.
终止经营指管理层已决定处置但尚未处置、或在本年度内已处置且此前曾产生损益的业务。构成终止经营要求该分部的资产、经营成果及投资/筹资活动可与公司其他部分区分。处置利得不贡献于未来收入/现金流，且只能在处置完成后（实现时）确认。分析师在预测盈利时可将其剔除。

Front:
Change in accounting policy vs change in accounting estimate
会计政策变更与会计估计变更
Back:
A change in accounting policy is a change in principles, bases, conventions, rules and practices (e.g., changing inventory costing method, or capitalizing rather than expensing). It requires retrospective application: prior-period statements are restated. A change in accounting estimate results from a change in management's judgment due to new information; it requires prospective application: prior statements are not restated and the change applies only to future statements. Both typically do not affect cash flow.
会计政策变更是对原则、基础、惯例、规则与方法的改变（如改变存货计价方法，或改费用化为资本化），须追溯适用：重述以前期间报表。会计估计变更源于新信息导致的管理层判断变化，采用未来适用法：不重述以前报表，变更仅影响未来期间。两者通常均不影响现金流。

Front:
Change in scope and change in exchange rates
合并范围变更与汇率变动
Back:
A change in scope occurs when an issuer acquires a controlling interest in another company and consolidates its financial statements as of the closing date. A change in exchange rates occurs with multinational companies' income statements. Accounting standards do not require issuers to disclose the effects of either scope or exchange rate changes on the financial statements or on individual items.
合并范围变更是指发行人在交割日取得另一公司控制权并合并其财务报表；汇率变动出现在跨国公司的利润表中。会计准则不要求发行人披露合并范围或汇率变动对财务报表或单个项目的影响。

Front:
Operating vs non-operating items: special cases
经营性与非经营性项目：特殊情形
Back:
Operating activities involve producing/delivering goods and providing services in the normal course of business; non-operating activities do not. Special treatments: gain/loss on disposal of fixed assets is recorded as an unusual or infrequent item but is still part of operating activities; interest expense and investment income are non-operating for a nonfinancial company but operating for a financial company; restructuring charges are operating under US GAAP but non-operating under IFRS.
经营活动指在正常经营过程中生产/交付商品和提供服务，反之则为非经营活动。特殊处理：固定资产处置损益作为异常或偶发项目列报，但仍属经营活动；利息费用与投资收益对非金融企业属非经营性，对金融企业则属经营性；重组费用在美国 GAAP 下属经营性，在 IFRS 下属非经营性。

Front:
EPS definition; simple vs complex capital structure
EPS 定义；简单与复杂资本结构
Back:
Earnings per share (EPS) is the share of a company's net income owned by common shareholders only. A simple capital structure contains no potentially convertible securities and reports only basic EPS. A complex capital structure contains potentially convertible securities that could convert into common stock and potentially dilute (reduce) EPS; such companies must also disclose diluted EPS, showing what EPS would be if all dilutive securities were converted.
每股收益（EPS）是公司净利润中归属于普通股股东的份额。简单资本结构不含潜在可转换证券，仅报告基本 EPS；复杂资本结构含可转换为普通股、可能稀释（摊薄）EPS 的潜在可转换证券，此类公司还须披露稀释 EPS，即假设所有稀释性证券全部转换后的 EPS。

Front:
Dilutive vs antidilutive securities
稀释性与反稀释性证券
Back:
Convertible securities give investors the right to convert into shares. If the opportunity cost of converting is small, investors would convert, diluting EPS, so the company reports diluted EPS (dilutive). If the opportunity cost is large, investors would not convert, so it does not dilute EPS and basic EPS = diluted EPS (antidilutive). If antidilutive securities were converted, they would actually increase EPS, which is why investors never convert them.
可转换证券赋予投资者转换为股票的权利。若转换的机会成本小，投资者会选择转换，从而稀释 EPS，公司须报告稀释 EPS（稀释性）；若机会成本大，投资者不会转换，EPS 不被稀释，基本 EPS＝稀释 EPS（反稀释性）。反稀释性证券若被转换反而会提高 EPS，这正是投资者永不转换的原因。

Front:
Basic EPS formula and weighted average shares
基本 EPS 公式与加权平均股数
Back:
Basic EPS does not consider any dilutive securities. Basic EPS = (Net income - Preferred dividends) / Weighted average number of common shares. The weighted average number of common shares = number of outstanding ordinary shares × the portion of the year they were outstanding. Two special cases require attention: a new share issue, and a stock split or stock dividend.
基本 EPS 不考虑任何稀释性证券：基本 EPS＝（净利润−优先股股利）/加权平均普通股数。加权平均普通股数＝流通在外普通股数×其当年流通时间占比。两个需注意的特殊情形：增发新股；股票分割或股票股利。

Front:
Weighted average shares: new issue
加权平均股数：增发新股
Back:
Newly issued shares enter the computation from the date of issuance, weighted by the fraction of the year outstanding. Example: 1,000,000 shares at the start plus 100,000 issued on 1 July gives weighted average = 1,000,000 + 100,000 × 6/12 = 1,050,000; with $1,000,000 net income, basic EPS = 1,000,000 / 1,050,000 = 0.952.
新发行股份自发行日起计入，按当年流通时间占比加权。示例：期初 1,000,000 股，7 月 1 日增发 100,000 股，加权平均＝1,000,000＋100,000×6/12＝1,050,000 股；净利润 1,000,000 美元时，基本 EPS＝1,000,000/1,050,000＝0.952 美元。

Front:
Weighted average shares: stock split / stock dividend
加权平均股数：股票分割/股票股利
Back:
A stock dividend distributes additional shares proportional to holdings (a 10% dividend gives a 100-share holder 10 more shares). A stock split divides each old share into new shares (a 2-for-1 split turns 100 shares into 200). A split or dividend is applied to all shares outstanding prior to it and to the beginning-of-period weighted average, but is NOT applied to shares issued or repurchased after the split/dividend date. Adjusted shares = original shares × (1 + stock dividend rate).
股票股利按持股比例派送额外股份（10% 股利使持有 100 股的股东多得 10 股）；股票分割将每股旧股拆分为若干新股（1 拆 2 使 100 股变为 200 股）。分割或股票股利须追溯适用于分割/派发前全部流通股及期初加权平均股数，但不适用于分割/派息日之后发行或回购的股份。调整后股数＝原股数×（1＋股票股利率）。

Front:
Diluted EPS: convertible preferred stock
稀释 EPS：可转换优先股
Back:
When a company has convertible preferred stock, Diluted EPS = Net income / (Weighted average shares + new common shares from conversion). Preferred dividends are NOT subtracted because conversion eliminates them. If preferred dividends are high, the opportunity cost of converting is large and the preferred is antidilutive. Quick check: if (preferred dividend / shares from conversion) < basic EPS, the convertible preferred is dilutive.
公司存在可转换优先股时，稀释 EPS＝净利润/（加权平均股数＋转换新增的普通股数）。优先股股利不再扣除，因为转换使其消失。若优先股股利很高，转换的机会成本大，该优先股为反稀释性。快速判断：若（优先股股利/转换所得股数）＜基本 EPS，则可转换优先股具稀释性。

Front:
Diluted EPS: convertible debt
稀释 EPS：可转换债券
Back:
When a company has convertible debt outstanding, Diluted EPS = (Net income + after-tax interest on convertible debt - preferred dividends) / (Weighted average shares + additional shares from conversion). The after-tax interest is added back because conversion eliminates the interest. Quick check: if (convertible debt interest × (1 - tax rate) / convertible debt shares) < basic EPS, the debt is dilutive. Example: after-tax interest = par × rate × (1 - t); diluted EPS uses the recomputed numerator and denominator, taken only if below basic EPS.
公司存在流通可转换债券时，稀释 EPS＝（净利润＋可转换债券税后利息−优先股股利）/（加权平均股数＋转换新增股数）。加回税后利息是因为转换使利息消失。快速判断：若（可转换债券利息×（1−税率）/转换所得股数）＜基本 EPS，则该债券具稀释性。示例：税后利息＝面值×票面利率×（1−t）；稀释 EPS 采用重算后的分子与分母，且仅当其低于基本 EPS 时才采用。

Front:
Diluted EPS: stock options and warrants (treasury stock method)
稀释 EPS：股票期权与认股权证（库存股法）
Back:
When a company has options/warrants, Diluted EPS = (Net income - preferred dividends) / (Weighted average shares + (new shares issued at exercise - shares repurchasable with cash received on exercise) × proportion of year outstanding). Shares repurchasable = exercise price × number of options / average market price. Options are dilutive only when market price > exercise price; if market price < exercise price they are antidilutive and diluted EPS = basic EPS.
公司存在期权/认股权证时，稀释 EPS＝（净利润−优先股股利）/〔加权平均股数＋（行权新发行的股数−用行权所得现金可回购的股数）×当年流通时间占比〕。可回购股数＝行权价×期权数量/平均市价。只有当市价＞行权价时期权才具稀释性；市价＜行权价时具反稀释性，稀释 EPS＝基本 EPS。

Front:
Diluted EPS with multiple potentially dilutive securities
存在多种潜在稀释性证券时的稀释 EPS
Back:
With convertible preferred, convertible debt, and options/warrants together: Diluted EPS = (Net income - preferred dividends + convertible preferred dividends + convertible debt interest × (1 - t)) / (Weighted average shares + shares from conv. preferred + shares from conv. debt + shares issuable from options). Each security must be examined separately to confirm it is actually dilutive (would reduce EPS) before including it.
可转换优先股、可转换债券和期权/认股权证并存时：稀释 EPS＝（净利润−优先股股利＋可转换优先股股利＋可转换债券利息×（1−t））/（加权平均股数＋可转换优先股转换股数＋可转换债券转换股数＋期权可发行股数）。每项证券须单独检验，确认其确实会稀释（降低）EPS 后方可纳入。

Front:
Common-size income statement
共同比利润表
Back:
A common-size income statement states each line as a percentage of sales (revenue). This facilitates comparison of firms across time periods and of firms of different sizes. For example, cost of sales, gross profit, and operating profit are each expressed as a percentage of total sales.
共同比利润表将各项目表示为销售额（收入）的百分比，便于同一公司跨期比较及不同规模公司之间比较。例如，销售成本、毛利润和经营利润均表示为销售总额的百分比。

Front:
Gross profit margin and net profit margin
毛利率与净利率
Back:
Gross profit margin = Gross profit / Revenue; it can be increased by raising prices or reducing production costs. Net profit margin = Net income / Revenue; it measures profit generated after considering all expenses. Both should be compared over time and with the firm's industry peers.
毛利率＝毛利润/收入，可通过提价或降低生产成本来提高；净利率＝净利润/收入，衡量扣除全部费用后创造的利润。两者都应进行跨期比较并与同业对比。

Front:
Comprehensive income and other comprehensive income (OCI)
综合收益与其他综合收益（OCI）
Back:
Under IFRS and GAAP, comprehensive income is the change in equity during a period from transactions and other events from non-owner sources: Comprehensive income = net income + other comprehensive income (OCI). OCI includes four types of items: foreign currency translation adjustments; unrealized gains/losses on derivatives accounted for as hedges; unrealized holding gains/losses on available-for-sale securities; and certain costs of defined benefit post-retirement plans not recognized in the current period.
在 IFRS 和 GAAP 下，综合收益是期间内非所有者来源的交易及其他事项引起的权益变动：综合收益＝净利润＋其他综合收益（OCI）。OCI 包括四类项目：外币折算调整；作为套期工具核算的衍生工具未实现损益；可供出售证券的未实现持有损益；以及设定受益退休后计划中当期未确认的某些成本。

Front:
Financial reporting quality vs. quality of reported results
财务报告质量与报告业绩的质量
Back:
Financial reporting quality refers to how well the reports conform to accounting standards and faithfully represent economic reality. Quality of reported results (earnings quality) refers to the level and sustainability of the actual economic performance. High reporting quality can accompany either high or low earnings quality.
财务报告质量指报告在多大程度上遵循会计准则并如实反映经济现实；报告业绩的质量（盈利质量）指实际经营业绩的水平与可持续性。高报告质量既可伴随高盈利质量，也可伴随低盈利质量。

Front:
Two qualities of high-quality (decision-useful) financial reporting
高质量（有助于决策）的财务报告的两个质量特征
Back:
High quality financial reporting must be decision useful, which requires: (1) Relevance — information is useful for users' decisions and must be material (its knowledge would likely affect decisions); and (2) Faithful representation — encompassing completeness, neutrality, and freedom from error.
高质量财务报告必须有助于决策，这要求：（1）相关性——信息有助于使用者决策且具有重要性（知悉该信息可能影响决策）；（2）如实反映——包括完整性、中立性和无差错。

Front:
Quality of earnings: sustainability and level
盈利质量：可持续性与水平
Back:
Earnings quality is judged on: (1) Sustainability — the proportion of reported earnings expected to continue in the future (e.g., earnings from core business); and (2) Level of earnings — reported earnings must be high enough to sustain the company's operations and existence (e.g., ROE greater than the required rate of return).
盈利质量从两方面判断：（1）可持续性——报告利润中预期未来能够延续的比例（如核心业务利润）；（2）利润水平——报告利润须足够高以维持公司的经营与存续（如 ROE 高于必要报酬率）。

Front:
Interaction of financial reporting quality and earnings quality
财务报告质量与盈利质量的相互作用
Back:
Low financial reporting quality impedes assessment of earnings quality and impedes valuation. High financial reporting quality enables assessment: when earnings quality is also high it increases company value, but when earnings quality is low it decreases company value.
低财务报告质量会妨碍对盈利质量的评估，也会妨碍估值。高财务报告质量使评估成为可能：盈利质量也高时，公司价值提升；盈利质量低时，公司价值下降。

Front:
Spectrum for assessing financial reporting quality (highest to worst)
财务报告质量评估谱系（最优到最差）
Back:
From highest to worst: (1) GAAP-compliant, earnings sustainable and adequate; (2) GAAP-compliant but earnings quality low (not sustainable/adequate); (3) GAAP-compliant but reporting choices and estimates are biased; (4) GAAP-compliant but earnings actively managed to increase, decrease, or smooth; (5) Not GAAP-compliant but numbers based on actual economic activities; (6) Not compliant and includes fictitious or fraudulent numbers.
从最优到最差：（1）符合 GAAP，盈利可持续且充足；（2）符合 GAAP，但盈利质量低（不可持续/不充足）；（3）符合 GAAP，但报告选择和估计存在偏向；（4）符合 GAAP，但主动管理利润以调高、调低或平滑；（5）不符合 GAAP，但数字基于真实经济活动；（6）不合规且包含虚构或欺诈数字。

Front:
Aggressive vs. conservative accounting choices
激进与保守的会计选择
Back:
Aggressive choices increase the company's reported performance and financial position in the current period and decrease earnings in future periods. Conservative choices decrease reported performance and financial position in the current period and increase future period earnings.
激进选择抬高当期报告的业绩与财务状况，降低未来期间利润；保守选择压低当期报告的业绩与财务状况，增加未来期间利润。

Front:
Examples: aggressive vs. conservative bias in accounting
示例：会计中的激进与保守偏向
Back:
Capitalizing a current period cost is aggressive (period cost down, net income up); expensing it immediately is conservative (period cost up, net income down). Straight-line depreciation is aggressive in early stages (lower depreciation expense, higher net income); accelerated depreciation is conservative early (higher depreciation expense, lower net income).
将当期支出资本化属激进（当期费用下降、净利润上升）；立即费用化属保守（当期费用上升、净利润下降）。直线折旧在前期属激进（折旧费用低、净利润高）；加速折旧在前期属保守（折旧费用高、净利润低）。

Front:
Is conservatism 'good'? Benefits and drawbacks
保守主义是“好”的吗？利与弊
Back:
Conservatism should not be seen as 'good'; it is a deviation from neutral reporting and faithful representation. Benefits: reducing possibility of litigation, reducing current period tax liability, and protecting those with less complete information. Drawback: it directly conflicts with neutrality, producing biased estimates of assets, liabilities, and earnings. Common conservative standards include research costs, litigation losses, and insurance recoverables.
保守主义不应被视为“好”的，它偏离了中立列报和如实反映。好处：降低涉诉可能性、减少当期税负、保护信息不充分的一方。弊端：与中立性直接冲突，导致对资产、负债和利润的有偏估计。常见的保守性准则处理包括研究支出、诉讼损失和保险理赔款。

Front:
Earnings smoothing
盈余平滑
Back:
Earnings smoothing involves employing conservative assumptions to understate performance when the company is actually doing well, then using aggressive assumptions when the company is not doing as well, producing a smoother earnings series than the unbiased path. Cookie jar reserve accounting is a case of earnings smoothing.
盈余平滑是指在公司实际业绩好时用保守假设低报业绩，在业绩不佳时用激进假设高报业绩，使利润序列比无偏轨迹更平滑。“甜饼罐”准备金会计就是盈余平滑的典型案例。

Front:
Big bath behavior
大清洗行为
Back:
Big bath behavior refers to the strategy of manipulating a company's income statement to make poor results look even worse (in a low-earning period), so that future periods appear better by comparison. Its effect is a conservative choice now and an aggressive boost later.
大清洗行为是指通过操纵公司的损益表，将不佳的业绩弄得更差（在低盈利时期），从而使未来期间相较之下显得更好的一种策略。其效果是现在采取保守选择，随后给予激进提振。

Front:
Fraud triangle: motivations and conditions for low-quality reporting
舞弊三角：低质量报告的动机与条件
Back:
Three conditions conducive to low-quality/fraudulent reporting: (1) Opportunity — weak internal controls, inadequate board oversight, or a large range of acceptable accounting treatments; (2) Motivation — mask poor performance, boost stock price, increase personal compensation, avoid debt covenant violation, exceed forecasts, or meet/beat expectations; (3) Rationalization — a story to justify breaking the rules.
促成低质量/舞弊报告的三个条件：（1）机会——内部控制薄弱、董事会监督不足或可选会计处理范围宽泛；（2）动机——掩盖不良业绩、推高股价、增加个人报酬、避免违反债务契约、超出预测或达到/超过市场预期；（3）合理化——为违规行为自圆其说的借口。

Front:
Four mechanisms that discipline financial reporting quality
约束财务报告质量的四种机制
Back:
(1) Markets — companies compete for capital and cost of capital relates to perceived risk, so they aim for high-quality reports to minimize long-term cost of capital; (2) Regulatory authorities — registration, disclosure/reporting requirements, management statements, signed statements, review processes, plus enforcement (fines, suspension); (3) Auditors; (4) Private contracts.
（1）市场——公司为资本而竞争，资本成本与被感知的风险相关，因此公司力求高质量报告以最小化长期资本成本；（2）监管机构——注册、披露/报告要求、管理层声明、签署声明、审查程序及执法（罚款、停牌）；（3）审计师；（4）私人合同。

Front:
Auditors and private contracts as discipline mechanisms (and limitations)
审计师与私人合同作为约束机制（及其局限）
Back:
Public companies must have statements audited by an independent auditor; private companies may obtain audits voluntarily or as required by capital providers. Under US GAAP, public firms also need an audit opinion on internal control effectiveness. Limitation: an unqualified ('clean') opinion is not a guarantee that no fraud occurred — it offers only reasonable assurance. Counterparties to private contracts have an incentive to ensure high-quality reporting.
公众公司的报表必须经独立审计师审计；私营公司可自愿或按资金提供方要求接受审计。美国 GAAP 下，公众公司还须就内部控制有效性取得审计意见。局限：无保留（“清洁”）意见并不保证没有舞弊——它仅提供合理保证。私人合同的交易对手有动力确保高质量报告。

Front:
Requirements for reporting non-GAAP measures
报告非 GAAP 指标的要求
Back:
Companies reporting non-GAAP measures must: display the most comparable GAAP measure with equal prominence; provide a management explanation of why the non-GAAP measure is useful; reconcile the differences between the non-GAAP and comparable GAAP measures; disclose other purposes for which the firm uses the measure; and include any items likely to recur, even those treated as nonrecurring, unusual, or infrequent.
报告非 GAAP 指标的公司必须：以同等显著程度列示最具可比性的 GAAP 指标；由管理层解释该非 GAAP 指标为何有用；调节非 GAAP 指标与可比 GAAP 指标之间的差异；披露公司使用该指标的其他目的；并纳入任何可能重复发生的项目，即使其被视为非经常性、异常或偶发项目。

Front:
Requirements for reporting non-IFRS measures
报告非 IFRS 指标的要求
Back:
IFRS require firms using non-IFRS measures to: define and explain the relevance of such non-IFRS measures; and reconcile the differences between the non-IFRS measure and the most comparable IFRS measure.
IFRS 要求使用非 IFRS 指标的公司：定义并解释该等非 IFRS 指标的相关性；调节非 IFRS 指标与最具可比性的 IFRS 指标之间的差异。

Front:
Revenue recognition techniques used to manage earnings
用于盈余管理的收入确认手法
Back:
Bill-and-hold: firm sells goods but keeps them at its location, so period-end inventory stays high, COGS is low, and net income and assets are recognized high. FOB shipping point recognizes revenue aggressively/earlier while FOB destination recognizes it later. Channel stuffing: in low-earning periods, overload distribution channels to raise current revenue (lowering future revenue); in high-earning periods, delay shipments/revenue to the next period.
开票留置：公司售出商品但将其留在自有场地，期末存货保持高位、销货成本偏低，净利润和资产被高报。FOB 起运点交货更早、更激进地确认收入，FOB 目的地交货则较晚确认。渠道压货：在低盈利期向分销渠道超量供货以抬高当期收入（透支未来收入）；在高盈利期则延迟发货/收入至下期。

Front:
Managing earnings via estimates of credit losses (allowance for bad debt)
通过信用损失估计（坏账准备）管理盈余
Back:
Decreasing the allowance for bad debt increases net receivables on the balance sheet and decreases expenses, raising net income. Increasing the allowance decreases net receivables and increases expenses, lowering net income.
减少坏账准备会增加资产负债表上的应收账款净额、减少费用，从而抬高净利润；增加坏账准备会减少应收账款净额、增加费用，从而压低净利润。

Front:
Managing earnings via the deferred tax valuation allowance
通过递延所得税估值备抵管理盈余
Back:
A valuation allowance reduces the carrying value of a deferred tax asset. Increasing the valuation allowance decreases the net deferred tax asset on the balance sheet and decreases net income for the period. Decreasing the valuation allowance increases the net deferred tax asset and increases net income.
估值备抵用于调减递延所得税资产的账面价值。增加估值备抵会减少资产负债表上递延所得税资产净额并减少当期净利润；减少估值备抵则增加递延所得税资产净额并增加净利润。

Front:
Depreciation, amortization/impairment, and inventory choices to manage results
通过折旧、摊销/减值和存货选择管理业绩
Back:
Depreciation methods and estimates of useful life and salvage value affect expenses and net income. Ignoring or delaying recognition of a goodwill impairment charge increases current-period earnings. The choice among FIFO, LIFO, and weighted-average inventory costing affects COGS, gross profit, gross margin, and earnings.
折旧方法及使用年限、残值估计会影响费用与净利润；忽视或延迟确认商誉减值会抬高当期利润；FIFO、LIFO 与加权平均存货计价方法的选择会影响销货成本、毛利润、毛利率和利润。

Front:
Capitalization, related-party transactions, and other cash flow effects
资本化、关联方交易与其他现金流影响
Back:
Capitalizing an expense creates an asset and spreads the net income impact over many years, and also affects cash flow classifications. Related-party transactions: if a public firm buys from a private supplier controlled by management, adjusting the transfer price shifts profits to manage reported earnings. Under IFRS, the ability to classify interest and dividends paid as CFO or CFF, and interest and dividends received as CFO or CFI, lets management manage reported operating cash flow.
将费用资本化会形成资产，把对净利润的影响分摊到多个年度，同时影响现金流分类。关联方交易：若公众公司向管理层控制的私营供应商采购，调整转让定价即可转移利润、操纵报告盈利。在 IFRS 下，已付利息和股利可归类为经营或筹资现金流，已收利息和股利可归类为经营或投资现金流，这使管理层得以管理报告的经营现金流。

Front:
Accounting warning signs of manipulation
盈余操纵的会计警示信号
Back:
Warning signs include: capitalization decisions, depreciation methods, useful lives, and salvage values out of line with comparable firms; net income not supported by operating cash flows; revenue growth out of line with peers, changes in or lack of transparency about revenue recognition; decreasing turnover ratios over time (receivables, inventory, total asset); fourth-quarter earnings patterns not due to seasonality; frequent nonrecurring items; bill-and-hold, barter, or related-party transactions; and emphasis on non-GAAP measures with minimal disclosure.
警示信号包括：资本化决策、折旧方法、使用年限和残值与可比公司不符；净利润缺乏经营现金流支撑；收入增长与同业背离、收入确认政策变更或透明度不足；周转率（应收账款、存货、总资产）随时间下降；第四季度盈利模式无法用季节性解释；频繁出现“非经常性”项目；开票留置、易货或关联方交易；强调非 GAAP 指标且披露极少。

Front:
Accounting profit vs. taxable income
会计利润与应纳税所得额
Back:
Accounting profit (pre-tax income) is profit recognized under financial reporting standards (IFRS/US GAAP). Taxable income is profit calculated under tax rules and is the base to which the tax rate is applied to get taxes payable. Differences in revenue/expense recognition between the two frameworks cause accounting profit to differ from taxable income.
会计利润（税前利润）是按财务报告准则（IFRS/美国 GAAP）确认的利润；应纳税所得额是按税法规则计算的利润，是适用税率据以计算应纳税额的基数。两套框架在收入/费用确认上的差异导致会计利润与应纳税所得额不同。

Front:
Taxes payable vs. income tax expense
应交所得税与所得税费用
Back:
Taxes payable (income tax payable) = Taxable income × Tax rate; it is the amount owed to tax authorities. Income tax expense = Taxes payable + Deferred tax expense; it is the amount recognized on the income statement. The two differ whenever there is a deferred tax expense (i.e., temporary differences exist).
应交所得税＝应纳税所得额×税率，是欠付税务机关的金额；所得税费用＝应交所得税＋递延所得税费用，是利润表中确认的金额。只要存在递延所得税费用（即存在暂时性差异），两者就不相等。

Front:
Temporary difference (definition)
暂时性差异（定义）
Back:
A temporary difference is a difference between taxable income and accounting profit that is expected to reverse in the future. It gives rise to deferred tax assets (DTA) or deferred tax liabilities (DTL).
暂时性差异是应纳税所得额与会计利润之间、预期未来会转回的差异，由此产生递延所得税资产（DTA）或递延所得税负债（DTL）。

Front:
Permanent difference (definition)
永久性差异（定义）
Back:
A permanent difference is a difference between taxable income and accounting profit that will not reverse in the future (e.g., non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income). It directly affects taxable income and causes the effective tax rate to differ from the statutory tax rate, but it does not create a DTA or DTL.
永久性差异是应纳税所得额与会计利润之间、未来不会转回的差异（如不可税前扣除的费用、免税收入）。它直接影响应纳税所得额，使实际税率不同于法定税率，但不产生 DTA 或 DTL。

Front:
P&L approach to deferred tax
递延所得税的利润表法
Back:
Under the profit-and-loss (P&L) approach, deferred tax expense is measured directly from the temporary difference in pre-tax income each period: Deferred tax expense = (Accounting profit − Taxable income) × Tax rate. This expense accumulates over time as the DTL/DTA balance.
在利润表（P&L）法下，递延所得税费用直接根据各期税前利润的暂时性差异计量：递延所得税费用＝（会计利润−应纳税所得额）×税率。该费用随时间累积，形成 DTL/DTA 余额。

Front:
Balance sheet approach to deferred tax
递延所得税的资产负债表法
Back:
Under the balance sheet (B/S) approach — the more commonly used method — DTL/DTA is measured from the temporary difference in account balances: DTL or DTA = |Carrying amount of asset/liability − Tax base| × Tax rate. The change in the DTA/DTL balance from period to period equals the deferred tax expense recognized in P&L.
在资产负债表（B/S）法——更常用的方法——下，DTL/DTA 根据账面余额的暂时性差异计量：DTL 或 DTA＝｜资产/负债账面价值−计税基础｜×税率。DTA/DTL 余额的期间变动额即为利润表中确认的递延所得税费用。

Front:
Statutory tax rate
法定税率
Back:
The statutory tax rate is the corporate income tax rate set by law in the country in which the company is domiciled.
法定税率是公司注册所在国法律规定的企业所得税税率。

Front:
Effective tax rate
实际税率
Back:
Effective tax rate = Income tax expense (reported on the income statement) / Pre-tax (accounting) income. It can differ from the statutory rate due to permanent differences, tax credits, foreign operations, and other adjustments.
实际税率＝所得税费用（利润表列报）/税前（会计）利润。由于永久性差异、税收抵免、境外经营及其他调整，实际税率可能不同于法定税率。

Front:
Cash tax rate
现金税率
Back:
Cash tax rate = Cash taxes actually paid during the period / Pre-tax income. It reflects the real cash tax burden as opposed to the accrual-based book tax expense.
现金税率＝当期实际缴纳的现金税款/税前利润。它反映真实的现金税负，有别于权责发生制下的账面所得税费用。

Front:
Reasons effective tax rate differs from statutory tax rate
实际税率与法定税率存在差异的原因
Back:
Differences can arise from: tax credits; withholding tax on dividends; adjustments related to prior years; expenses not deductible for tax purposes; and the company operating outside the country where it is domiciled.
差异可能来自：税收抵免；股利预提税；与以前年度相关的调整；不可税前扣除的费用；以及公司在注册国以外经营。

Front:
Deferred tax liability (DTL) — definition
递延所得税负债（DTL）——定义
Back:
A deferred tax liability is the amount of income taxes payable in future periods as a result of taxable temporary differences.
递延所得税负债是因应纳税暂时性差异而在未来期间应缴纳的所得税金额。

Front:
Deferred tax asset (DTA) — definition
递延所得税资产（DTA）——定义
Back:
A deferred tax asset is the amount of income taxes recoverable (i.e., tax savings) in future periods as a result of deductible temporary differences.
递延所得税资产是因可抵扣暂时性差异而在未来期间可收回（即节税）的所得税金额。

Front:
Tax base of an asset
资产的计税基础
Back:
The tax base of an asset is the amount that will be deducted (expensed) on the tax return in the future as the economic benefits of the asset are realized.
资产的计税基础是随着资产经济利益实现、未来在纳税申报中可扣除（费用化）的金额。

Front:
Tax base of a liability
负债的计税基础
Back:
Tax base of liabilities = Carrying value of the liability − amounts that will be deductible on the tax return in the future. For revenue received in advance, tax base = carrying value − amount of revenue that will not be taxed in the future.
负债的计税基础＝负债账面价值−未来纳税申报中可扣除的金额。对于预收收入：计税基础＝账面价值−未来不再征税的收入金额。

Front:
DTL/DTA rule for an asset temporary difference
资产暂时性差异的 DTL/DTA 判定规则
Back:
For an asset: if Carrying amount > Tax base, future accounting profit will be lower than future taxable income (pay more tax later) → deferred tax liability. If Carrying amount < Tax base, future accounting profit will be higher than future taxable income (pay less tax later) → deferred tax asset.
对资产而言：若账面价值＞计税基础，未来会计利润将低于应纳税所得额（未来多缴税）→递延所得税负债；若账面价值＜计税基础，未来会计利润将高于应纳税所得额（未来少缴税）→递延所得税资产。

Front:
DTL/DTA rule for a liability temporary difference
负债暂时性差异的 DTL/DTA 判定规则
Back:
